builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
summary: HarnessFlow replaces the manual, ad-hoc design of agent scaffolding and tool-use loops with an automated Monte Carlo Tree Search over executable harness code. The approach requires a budget of approximately 15 end-to-end evaluation cycles per task and the operational cost of running a coding agent to generate and test candidate harnesses. Reliance on archived execution history can lead to overfitting to specific benchmarks or failure to generalize to unseen environments, and the MCTS search may converge on suboptimal harness designs if the evaluation budget is too constrained or the coding agent produces buggy code.
rationale: The method offers measurable quality improvements and reduced execution costs but requires rigorous validation on the user's specific workloads to ensure the automated search does not overfit to benchmark idiosyncrasies.

claims.statement: HarnessFlow replaces the manual, ad-hoc design of agent scaffolding and tool-use loops with an automated Monte Carlo Tree Search over executable harness code. The approach requires a budget of approximately 15 end-to-end evaluation cycles per task and the operational cost of running a coding agent to generate and test candidate harnesses. Reliance on archived execution history can lead to overfitting to specific benchmarks or failure to generalize to unseen environments, and the MCTS search may converge on suboptimal harness designs if the evaluation budget is too constrained or the coding agent produces buggy code.

The optimized harnesses achieve an average score of 69.48%, outperforming initial harnesses and Meta-Harness by 10.89 and 3.95 percentage points, respectively, while incurring lower average per-task execution costs than hand-engineered baselines.
